source_notes: Locked Sept22 whole bird: compact folded oval shield, comparatively round integrated chest, dense overlapping scalloped head/crown plates, contoured pale brow plate with repeated fasteners, deeply recessed amber optic dominating face, dark jaw opening with several nested curved plates, broad substantial segmented toes and heavy conical claws.

July controls head only: long deep hook bill and swept overlapping crown; structured crescent cheek/mandible framing a dark opening; pale brow follows head curve around the socket rather than a plain top panel. Exclude July body and long wings.

FirstChoice 0.5,2,4,6.5s frames maintain layered plate/fastener response, regional dark patina with worn edges, amber eye focus, broad planted feet and coherent dense machinery. These are static frame judgments, not motion acceptance.

Maker source shows bronze/green newly fabricated regional metal and dark glass eye; Mechanic source shows age and repair character; Advanced source retains inherited surfaces with awake optic. Source lighting differs so precise colors are uncertain.
candidate_notes: At normal whole-bird scale, all three candidate eras remain much more upright, with a prominent vertically elongated front breast ending in a narrow point and a comparatively small rear body. No approved-pose change is demanded, but the locked target mismatch remains visible.

The new breast overlap is visually connected from throat into breast and reduces the previous loose small-scale plating; this is a meaningful study gain. The broader smoother panels also lose source riveted subdivision and compact flow.

Bright pale gold forehead panel now dominates all eras; the recess optic is circular and Advanced amber is restrained and visible at whole scale, but the brow shape/material hierarchy does not closely match the scoped source. Maker/Mechanic visually have dark eye centers.
Crown uses sparse long pointed pieces with large open construction below them; head/cheek hardware is coarse and smooth compared with source layered nested plates and small fasteners.

Feet closeups reveal broad flattened cover strips across the toe dorsum and smooth short talons. The source feet have individually articulated cylindrical toe volume and much stronger claw mass. Existing candidate stance anchors cannot settle this visual criterion.
Maker and Mechanic images show almost no distinguishable whole-scale finish/repair evolution. Advanced differs principally in optic, leaving the era finish requirement unmet to my visual reading.

Native 135/180 rear views and browser orbit expose a large empty-looking head/neck opening and deep gaps around rear shoulders. Unseen source back geometry cannot be inferred; visible candidate incompleteness nevertheless weakens coherent cinematic construction.

Actual browser neutral/exhibit captures retain the same whole-shape mismatch and flatten/dull the surface response; illustrated native-image fallback is visibly stronger in shadow grounding. Pixel parity is not expected, but target screen presence is not established in either.
